newsitem.title: USA: Moler fields senators' questions for US energy job.
newsitem.headline: Moler fields senators' questions for US energy job.

text.p: President Clinton's choice to be deputy energy secretary Tuesday said the administration considers a proposed sale of $1.1 billion of oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve in fiscal 2002 "a budget placeholder."

Elizabeth Moler, currently chairman of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, also told reporters she was not aware of any proposal for earlier SPR sales in the deal to balance the budget that the White House and Congress reached last week.
The Senate Energy Committee held a confirmation hearing for Moler to be deputy energy secretary, and indicated she would have little trouble getting the job.
"Even though this is not a business meeting, your nomination in my opinion is a certainty," Committee Chairman Frank Murkowski, an Alaska Republican, told Moler.
Other committee members, Republicans and Democrats, also praised Moler, who had been expected to be named to the top Energy Department job until Clinton made a surprise nomination of Federico Pena.
Moler would replace Deputy Secretary Charles Curtis, who chose to leave the department.
A committee staffer said the panel could vote on Moler's nomination as early as next Wednesday if her answers to committee members' written questions are delivered in time.
Responding to Murkowski, Moler said she hoped the proposed SPR oil sale for 2002 "will not be necessary," and said it has been called a "placeholder."

Murkowski asked Moler to "use your influence" to oppose further sales of oil from the SPR, which is intended to keep a reserve that is large enough to help stabilize markets in case of import supply disruptions.

Moler also fielded a number of questions on the need for interim storage of radioactive waste from commercial utility nuclear power plants, and said she was "certainly aware of the continuing need to finallly come to grips with the high-level nuclear waste issue."
The administration opposes a bill pushed by Murkowski to build a temporary dump in Nevada, near the site under consideration for a permanent repository.
Moler also said one of the reasons she wanted the Energy Department post was to continue her involvement in the electric utility deregulation issue.
She said an "interagency process is underway, but is by no means concluded now" on the administration's position in the complex issue.
"If confirmed, I would happily attempt to be in the middle of that process," she said.
